newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes $3 down, confirms contango.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes $3 down, confirms contango.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures confirmed a rare midwinter shift into contango by sliding $3 a tonne on Friday, pressured by mild temperatures in both Europe and Northeastern United States, traders said.
Front month March finished at $170.50 after hitting a seven-month, spot contract low of $169.75. That was the lowest since July 1, when the front month touched $167.50 and closed at $171.75.
March recorded a $1 contango to April, which last traded at $171.50. May finished at $172.25.
March recorded a 25 cents contango to April on Thursday.
"It's the mild weather, no German buying and the movement in the dollar preventing buyers getting into the market -- the same factors we've seen for the past $40 worth of movement," a trader said.
Forecasts for higher than normal temperatures in the Northeast U.S., the world's largest energy market, and warmer weather in northwest Europe were pressuring heating oil prices, dealers said.
Traders added that one broker drew attention by aggressively trading March down throughout the day, apparently aiming at a move towards $165. Support after that would come at around $160.
IPE Brent crude trimmed losses, moving back to the middle of a 19-cent range on the back of light short-covering encouraged by a firmer tone on U.S. products markets.
April Brent was 22 cents weaker at $19.86 a barrel by 1739 GMT, 14 cents off the high and 10 cents off the session low.
"There's been a bit of short-covering. The feeling is that (NYMEX) unleaded has seen the lows and should range-trade for the rest of the day," said a broker.
Support was pegged at $19.75, where the bottom of a six-week downtrend channel crosses, and then at $19.70, another previous low from last August, brokers said.
Deeper support was seen at $19.50 a barrel.
